title: FromStr Interface
concept: The FromStr interface enables parsing strings into your type — `let x: MyType = "value".parse()?` — the gateway from text to typed data.
why: Most user input arrives as strings. FromStr standardizes string parsing, making your types instantly compatible with config files, CLI args, and APIs.
tips: FromStr is THE interface for parsing — implement it for any type that has a string representation
Use `.parse()` with type annotation — the compiler infers the target type
Return descriptive errors — 'invalid format at position 3' is better than 'parse error'
Implement FromStr for your domain types — it enables seamless CLI arg parsing
common_mistakes: Not handling whitespace in parsing — trim() strings before parsing numbers
Assuming the entire string is consumed — check for leftover characters after parsing
Using parse() without type annotation — add `:MyType` after the variable or on the let binding
